Topic: Useful homeowner lessons about cockroaches in Central Texas. Do not use the same publication twice (including mirrors). Use only identification, behavior or practical nonchemical prevention; no medical, dosing, mixing or product-specific directions. Explain Central Texas applicability and limits. Each card needs 1-4 supported facts with short EXACT quotes, at most 25 quoted words total per publication. Quotes will be checked by fetching the page independently. Use 'undated' if no date is available. Do not use search snippets as page evidence. The lesson field is Drew's source preview: one or two short plain-English sentences about what the source teaches and what the video could explain, at most four sentences and 600 characters. No hooks, jargon, headings or line breaks. Prefer detailed biology and original research over shallow FAQs. Before offering a source, assess whether it can support a longer educational explanation: a mechanism, useful observation and clear limits, or credible primary research that could supply the depth. Describe its educational depth naturally in the short lesson preview. A hook must be supportable by the main source itself. If fewer sources exist, return fewer; do not invent. RESEARCH BRIEF:
# Research brief: useful pest education for customers

**Find practical lessons a pest professional could explain to a homeowner. Show five short source previews; save every source Drew likes and research the next pest once the current queue has at least three. Writing is active: choose the source, then the hook, then a full narration.**

**Start rule:** making an episode and stocking the source queue are separate tasks. Use an already approved queued source for an episode when available; do not repeat discovery automatically. For new choices, send [this explicit request and apply these source criteria](../mp3-system/source-research.md). A source-research schedule is not yet chosen.

## Teaching target

Drew's example is a dog trainer teaching owners while working with their dog. Deep Six's equivalent is understandable pest education: what the homeowner notices, what it means, why it happens and what a sensible next step looks like. The finished content will use AI visuals and original explanations, rather than pretending Deep Six filmed another professional's visit.

Prefer one useful, visual lesson over a list of trivia or a sales pitch. A real pest professional's demonstration can provide a lesson, not merely a hook template. Keep the original source attached and distinguish what the creator actually demonstrates from your interpretation. Explain it in original words; do not assume permission to reuse their footage or script.

## Whiteboard flow

**Cron or on demand → choose pest needing sources → research through crawler when ready → check content and evidence → show five source summaries → Drew likes or skips → save liked sources → update pest rotation.**

On-demand research exists. Cron is planned, not activated. Drew has confirmed the crawler is ready. Use [the repeatable crawler procedure](../mp3-system/crawler-flow.md) for source discovery and later supporting science. Its authenticated API is reachable; the runner now emits crawler requests and imports checked results. The session agent operates the crawler. Do not claim a platform was accessed when it was not.

## Where lessons can come from

| Source type | Useful material | Current status |
|---|---|---|
| Web articles and blogs | Clear explanations, photographs, identification and practical prevention | Trusted public pages/PDFs work now. The automatic validator still uses its configured publisher allowlist; arbitrary blogs are not yet enabled. |
| Educational pest-control accounts and channels | Professional demonstrations and customer explanations | A desired creator/source category across platforms. Verify expertise, actual content and limits; not connected automatically yet. |
| Reddit | Real homeowner questions, recurring confusion, and useful expert responses | Planned. Drew reports supplying cookies to the crawler agent; this content runner's access and quality are unverified. An anecdote or vote count alone is not factual validation. |
| Facebook | Possible professional teaching posts or videos | Pending crawler access and a trial of content quality. Drew reports cookies supplied to that agent. |
| X / Twitter | Possible professional explanations and demonstrations | Pending access and a trial of content quality. Drew plans to provide cookies to the crawler agent. |
| YouTube videos and Shorts | In-depth lessons, visual demonstrations and short explanations | Pending YouTube research tools/transcript ingestion. Do not claim to watch video from its title or description. |

Cookies and other credentials stay with the crawler owner. This project stores access status only, never credential values. Do not inspect or copy them.

## Selection and evidence

- Stay on the requested pest. Prior liked ant sources should help identify useful teaching approaches, not force later searches back to ants.
- Prefer original sources, identifiable expertise and a concrete homeowner question. Check the actual relevant passage or demonstration, species and Central Texas applicability. Mark dates and limitations honestly.
- Keep the useful explanation and its factual support separate from popularity. A compelling creator is not automatically right; a social question can inspire a lesson that is then checked against reliable pest evidence.
- Record the original URL, creator/publisher, platform, pest group and species, useful lesson, checked date, evidence passages or video timestamps, what was actually read/watched, limits and prior-use status. Future platform adapters must preserve this evidence; the current runner handles article/PDF cards.
- Show five numbered source links with normally one or two sentences each, maximum four, explaining what the content would teach. No hook writing in this review.

## Queue, feedback and rotation

Save every explicitly liked source, not just the first one. The decision's `numbers` are all positive selections; `first_number` says which to use first. A single chosen `number` is also positive. Unmentioned choices are neutral. Do not invent a reason for a skip. Source feedback guides research; hook feedback stays separate.

The working grouping is broad pests: all ant types count under **ants**, with the actual species preserved on each card. This is a stated default, awaiting any correction from Drew. Working order: **ants → cockroaches → termites → mosquitoes → rodents → spiders → scorpions → bed bugs → fleas and ticks → stinging insects → wildlife**, then back around. The order is an implementation default, not a priority ranking supplied by Drew.

Count distinct liked sources that are queued or currently in use. Once a group has three or more, move to the next group needing sources. Do not discard a fourth source liked in the same batch. Merely finding or displaying sources does not meet the target. Finished sources stay in history but stop counting toward ready inventory, so a later rotation can replenish that pest. If every group is stocked, stop new research until a group needs more.

The decision was sources **1, 2, 4 and 5 liked, source 1 first**. Source 3 was not selected; that is not a rejection. Source 1 has an approved script and MP3 and remains reserved pending a finished MP4. Only final MP4 completion marks it used. Three other ant sources remain queued; next research is cockroaches. [Current start-to-MP3 flow](../mp3-system/README.md).

Narration preference update: prioritize useful, less-obvious facts homeowners are unlikely to know. Favor Texas-relevant evidence. Findings from elsewhere can support shared biology when applicability is explained, but do not present a state-specific measurement as a Texas result or describe imported fire ants as native. Drew expressed uncertainty about out-of-state framing, not an absolute ban.

Use Drew's source preferences to guide what you research and recommend. A source choice is a positive signal; unchosen options are not automatically disliked. A skipped batch is a weak signal with no known reason unless Drew stated one. Follow explicit comments most closely, with later corrections taking precedence. Keep a varied shortlist and preserve evidence standards. Hook/narration rejections are not source rejections. Prior summaries are taste context, not evidence for new facts.
